hero.title: Sri Gupta: The Dynasty Founder
hero.description: Sri Gupta laid the foundational stone of the Gupta Empire, transitioning India from the post-Mauryan fragmentation toward the classical Golden Age.

timeline.title: The Chronological Framework
timeline.description: The rise of the Guptas occurred in the vacuum left by the declining Kushanas.

cards.details: Sri Gupta rules as a local chieftain, likely a feudatory of the Later Kushanas in the Magadha region.

items.title: S-G-C (Small Gupta Chain)
items.decryption: Remember the sequence of the first three rulers to avoid confusion between Sri Gupta and Chandragupta.

items: Do not confuse Sri Gupta with Chandragupta Maurya; they belong to completely different eras.
Sri Gupta was a 'Maharaja', not a 'Maharajadhiraja'. This title confirms his status as a subordinate ruler/feudatory.

sections.title: 1. Core Study Notes
sections.content:
Geography

  • Core: Magadha (Modern Bihar)
  • Expansion: Limited to Bengal/Bihar border

Personalities

  • Sri Gupta: Founder
  • I-Tsing: Chinese traveler who documented Sri Gupta

Core Historical Analysis

  • Epigraphic Evidence: Mentioned in the Poona Copper Plate of Prabhavatigupta.
  • Travelogue Account: The Chinese traveler I-Tsing (7th Century CE) refers to 'Che-li-ki-to' (Sri-Gupta) who built a temple for Chinese pilgrims near Mrigasikhavana.
  • Political Status: Feudatory nature proven by the title 'Maharaja'.
SourceDescription
I-TsingMentions 'Che-li-ki-to' as the founder
PrabhavatiguptaMentions Sri Gupta as the first ancestor

practiceQuestions.q: Who is recognized as the founder of the Gupta dynasty?
practiceQuestions.sol: Sri Gupta is universally recognized in epigraphical records, such as the Poona copper plate of Prabhavatigupta, as the founder of the Gupta dynasty. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 History / Epigraphical Evidence]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the royal title generally held by Sri Gupta as mentioned in early epigraphs?
practiceQuestions.sol: Sri Gupta and his successor Ghatotkacha held the modest title of 'Maharaja', indicating that they were minor local rulers or feudatories initially. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 Themes in Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q: Which Chinese traveler's account mentions a Chinese pilgrim visiting a temple built by 'Che-li-ki-to' (Sri Gupta)?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Chinese pilgrim I-tsing (Yijing), who visited India around 671-695 CE, recorded the account of 'Che-li-ki-to' (Sri Gupta) constructing a temple for Chinese Buddhist pilgrims near Mrikhavana. [Primary Reference: Archaeological Survey of India / Accounts of I-tsing]

practiceQuestions.q: According to I-tsing's accounts, Sri Gupta's temple was built for Buddhist pilgrims from which foreign country?
practiceQuestions.sol: I-tsing explicitly noted that the temple was built by the king 'Sri Gupta' for the use of pilgrims coming from China. [Primary Reference: Ancient Indian History Sources, Majumdar]

practiceQuestions.q: Who succeeded Sri Gupta as the second ruler of the Gupta dynasty?
practiceQuestions.sol: Ghatotkacha was the son and immediate successor of Sri Gupta, maintaining the title of 'Maharaja'. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 History]

practiceQuestions.q: Approximate period for the beginning of Sri Gupta's reign is generally placed around which century?
practiceQuestions.sol: Sri Gupta's reign is generally placed in the late 3rd century CE (approx. 240–280 CE) before his son Ghatotkacha and grandson Chandragupta I expanded the realm. [Primary Reference: Upinder Singh, A History of Ancient and Early Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q: In which region was the early core territory of the Gupta empire under Sri Gupta likely located?
practiceQuestions.sol: Historians generally associate the early territorial footprint of Sri Gupta with parts of present-day Bengal and Bihar, as indicated by I-tsing's description and early copper plate inscriptions. [Primary Reference: R.S. Sharma, India's Ancient Past]

practiceQuestions.q: What designation is used for Sri Gupta in the genealogical lists of the Gupta inscriptions (such as the Allahabad Pillar Inscription)?
practiceQuestions.sol: In official genealogies, the Gupta line begins with 'Maharaja Sri-Gupta', denoting his foundational status with the title Maharaja. [Primary Reference: Corpus Inscriptionum Indicarum Vol. III]

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following dynasties was preceded by the rise of the Guptas under Sri Gupta in northern India?
opts: Kushanas / Later Kushanas and local powers
practiceQuestions.sol: The Guptas emerged in the political vacuum created after the decline of the Kushana empire and the fragmentation of northern India among various local powers. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 History]

practiceQuestions.q: The term 'Mrikhavana', associated with Sri Gupta's Buddhist establishment, refers to what?
practiceQuestions.sol: According to I-tsing, Sri Gupta endowed land and a temple situated at a deer park/forest area known as Mrikhavana for Chinese pilgrims. [Primary Reference: ASI Epigraphical Reports]

practiceQuestions.q: Why did Sri Gupta and Ghatotkacha adopt the title 'Maharaja' instead of the imperial 'Maharajadhiraja'?
opts: They were subordinate rulers or local chieftains under a higher sovereign authority initially.
They rejected royal titles due to religious asceticism.
The title 'Maharajadhiraja' had been abolished by the Mauryas.
Foreign invaders prohibited them from using higher titles.
practiceQuestions.sol: The use of the title 'Maharaja' indicates that Sri Gupta and Ghatotkacha were minor independent or subordinate local chiefs (likely under powers like the Later Kushanas or Murundas) before Chandragupta I assumed the imperial title 'Maharajadhiraja'. [Primary Reference: R.S. Sharma, Comprehensive History of India]

practiceQuestions.q: How does the travel account of I-tsing help historians reconstruct the chronology and existence of Sri Gupta?
opts: It provides an independent foreign chronological anchor dating Sri Gupta to roughly 500 years before I-tsing's visit.
It offers the exact birth and death dates of Sri Gupta recorded in stone.
It lists the military conquests of Sri Gupta against foreign nations.
It describes the tax collection system implemented by Sri Gupta.
practiceQuestions.sol: I-tsing noted that 'Che-li-ki-to' ruled about 500 years before his time, which helped scholars correlate indigenous epigraphic lists with external historical timelines. [Primary Reference: A.L. Basham, The Wonder That Was India]

practiceQuestions.q: What role did patronage of religious institutions play for early Gupta rulers like Sri Gupta?
opts: It helped legitimize their growing political authority and secure social support across communities.
It was purely done to extract heavy taxes from monastic lands.
It was mandated by the Mauryan legal code.
It served solely as a military alliance against western satraps.
practiceQuestions.sol: Endowing land and building facilities for religious groups (such as Buddhist temples by Sri Gupta) was a key mechanism for emerging rulers to gain legitimacy, moral authority, and socioeconomic integration. [Primary Reference: Romila Thapar, Early India]

practiceQuestions.q: Why is the transition from Sri Gupta to Chandragupta I considered a crucial evolutionary trend in ancient Indian polity?
opts: It marks the evolution of a local chiefdom into an imperial sovereignty through strategic expansion and matrimonial alliances.
It represents the shift from a monarchy to a democratic republic.
It denotes the complete eradication of Buddhism in favor of Jainism.
It signifies the relocation of the capital from Pataliputra to Taxila.
practiceQuestions.sol: The early phase under Sri Gupta and Ghatotkacha was marked by local rule ('Maharaja'), which transformed into full imperial stature ('Maharajadhiraja') under Chandragupta I, catalyzed by the Licchavi alliance. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 History]

practiceQuestions.q: In what manner did the political fragmentation of post-Mauryan India facilitate the emergence of dynastic founders like Sri Gupta?
opts: The collapse of central imperial control created numerous power vacuums allowing regional leaders to consolidate local territories.
Foreign powers directly appointed regional Indian founders to maintain peace.
Guilds of merchants elected kings democratically in northern India.
Religious leaders transferred absolute political power to monastic heads.
practiceQuestions.sol: Post-Mauryan northern India saw the rise of regional principalities and chieftains. The weakening of overarching empires enabled figures like Sri Gupta to establish small autonomous domains that later expanded. [Primary Reference: Bipan Chandra, India's Ancient Past]

practiceQuestions.q: How do epigraphical genealogies reconstruct the early Gupta rulers when primary coins or direct inscriptions from Sri Gupta's reign are sparse?
opts: Through retrofitted genealogical prasastis issued by later monarchs like Samudragupta and Kumaragupta.
Through foreign Roman trade manifests exclusively.
Through oral traditions transcribed in the Mughal era.
Through archaeological excavations of Harappan sites.
practiceQuestions.sol: Later Gupta inscriptions (such as the Allahabad Pillar Inscription and Nalanda/ Gaya copper plates) meticulously trace ancestry back to Sri Gupta and Ghatotkacha to establish dynastic legitimacy. [Primary Reference: D.C. Sircar, Select Inscriptions]

practiceQuestions.q: What does the existence of the Buddhist temple built by Sri Gupta for Chinese pilgrims signify regarding cultural exchange during the 3rd century CE?
opts: India maintained active cross-border religious and intellectual connections with East Asia even during early regional state formations.
Buddhism was exclusively patronized by foreign invaders rather than indigenous rulers.
Trade routes were closed to religious travelers.
Sri Gupta was a direct vassal of the Chinese Tang dynasty.
practiceQuestions.sol: The account demonstrates that international Buddhist networks and pilgrimage routes linked India with China well before the peak of the Gupta empire, and local rulers actively engaged with foreign religious visitors. [Primary Reference: Himanshu Ray, Winds of Change]

practiceQuestions.q: In the context of ancient Indian state formation, what differentiates a 'Maharaja' status from a 'Maharajadhiraja' status?
opts: 'Maharaja' denoted a subordinate or petty regional chief, whereas 'Maharajadhiraja' signified an independent imperial monarch of kings.
'Maharaja' was a title reserved exclusively for military generals.
'Maharajadhiraja' was used only by Buddhist monks.
There was no political or hierarchical difference between the two titles.
practiceQuestions.sol: Epigraphical studies show that imperial families often started with the modest 'Maharaja' title while acknowledging overlords, later graduating to 'Maharajadhiraja' (King of Kings) upon achieving full sovereignty. [Primary Reference: Epigraphia Indica]

practiceQuestions.q: How did the economic foundation under Sri Gupta likely support the subsequent imperial takeoff of the Guptas?
opts: Through control over fertile agrarian tracts and emerging trade corridors in the Gangetic basin.
Through heavy maritime raiding of Roman trade ships.
Through the monopoly of gold minting imported from Africa.
Through mandatory tribute collection from Central Asian empires.
practiceQuestions.sol: The early core region in eastern/central Gangetic plains provided a stable agrarian surplus and commercial linkages, which served as the economic bedrock for later military expansion. [Primary Reference: R.S. Sharma, Indian Feudalism / Early Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q: What is the primary significance of identifying 'Che-li-ki-to' with Sri Gupta in Indological studies?
opts: It bridges the gap between indigenous genealogical records and foreign eyewitness accounts, establishing historical anchoring.
It proves that Sri Gupta migrated to China and ruled there.
It invalidates all domestic epigraphs regarding the Gupta ancestry.
It confirms that Sanskrit was the official court language in China.
practiceQuestions.sol: Identifying I-tsing's 'Che-li-ki-to' with Sri Gupta gives historians a vital external chronological anchor and confirms the dynasty's engagement with religious philanthropy. [Primary Reference: J.F. Fleet, Corpus Inscriptionum Indicarum]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Sri Gupta, the founder of the Gupta dynasty:
1. He is explicitly mentioned in epigraphical records such as the Poona copper plate of Prabhavatigupta as the first ruler of the dynasty.
2. He held the imperial title of 'Maharajadhiraja' right from the beginning of his reign.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: The genealogical lists in Gupta inscriptions and grants (like the Poona copper plate) trace the dynasty back to Sri Gupta. Statement 2 is incorrect: Sri Gupta held the modest title of 'Maharaja', not 'Maharajadhiraja', which was assumed later by Chandragupta I. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 History]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about the foreign accounts concerning Sri Gupta:
1. The Chinese pilgrim Fa-Hien gave a detailed account of Sri Gupta building a Buddhist temple.
2. The traveler I-tsing referred to the founder of the Gupta dynasty as 'Che-li-ki-to'.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect: Fa-Hien visited India during the reign of Chandragupta II, not Sri Gupta, and did not write about Sri Gupta. Statement 2 is correct: I-tsing recorded that 'Che-li-ki-to' built a temple for Chinese pilgrims about 500 years before his time. [Primary Reference: Archaeological Survey of India Reports]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the successor and early governance of the Gupta dynasty:
1. Ghatotkacha was the immediate successor of Sri Gupta and also held the title of 'Maharaja'.
2. During the reigns of both Sri Gupta and Ghatotkacha, extensive gold coinage was minted carrying their personal portraits.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Ghatotkacha succeeded Sri Gupta and retained the title 'Maharaja'. Statement 2 is incorrect: No coins have been discovered belonging to Sri Gupta or Ghatotkacha; extensive gold coinage began only with Chandragupta I and Samudragupta. [Primary Reference: Altekar, The Coinage of the Gupta Empire]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about the geopolitical environment during Sri Gupta's era:
1. The Guptas rose to prominence in the region covering parts of Bengal and Bihar after the decline of the Kushana empire.
2. Sri Gupta successfully conquered the whole of southern India and established suzerainty over the Pallavas.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: The early Gupta base was localized in parts of Bengal and Bihar following the post-Kushana political fragmentation. Statement 2 is incorrect: Sri Gupta was a local chief with a modest territory; southern conquests were achieved much later by Samudragupta. [Primary Reference: R.S. Sharma, India's Ancient Past]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding epigraphical sources mentioning Sri Gupta:
1. The Allahabad Pillar Inscription of Samudragupta starts its royal genealogy directly by mentioning Sri Gupta.
2. Epigraphs from the Gupta period provide precise birth and death dates for Sri Gupta down to the exact day.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: The Allahabad Pillar Inscription (Prashasti) of Samudragupta begins the royal genealogy by mentioning 'Maharaja Sri-Gupta' as the first ancestor. Statement 2 is incorrect: Gupta inscriptions do not give exact birth or death dates for Sri Gupta; his chronology is estimated through comparative historical and foreign sources. [Primary Reference: Corpus Inscriptionum Indicarum Vol. III]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the cultural and religious activities associated with Sri Gupta:
1. I-tsing noted that Sri Gupta granted land and a village for the maintenance of a Buddhist temple built for pilgrims from China.
2. Sri Gupta converted to Buddhism and banned all Brahmanical practices within his kingdom.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: I-tsing recorded that the land and temple were endowed by King Sri Gupta for Chinese pilgrims. Statement 2 is incorrect: There is no historical evidence that Sri Gupta banned Brahmanical practices; early Gupta rulers followed a policy of religious tolerance and patronage towards multiple sects. [Primary Reference: Ancient Indian History Sources, Majumdar]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about the transition from Sri Gupta's rule to the Imperial Gupta age:
1. The transition involved expanding territorial control from local chiefdoms in eastern India to the Gangetic heartland.
2. The matrimonial alliance with the Licchavis under Chandragupta I was vital in elevating the Gupta status from 'Maharaja' to 'Maharajadhiraja'.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct: The Guptas expanded their small local base in eastern India into an empire, and the strategic marriage of Chandragupta I to Kumaradevi of the Licchavi clan immensely boosted their political clout, enabling the adoption of 'Maharajadhiraja'. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 Themes in Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the historiography of Sri Gupta:
1. Modern historians rely entirely on Greek accounts by Megasthenes to reconstruct the reign of Sri Gupta.
2. The name 'Sri Gupta' appears as the prime progenitor in almost all official Gupta dynastic inscriptions.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect: Megasthenes lived during the Mauryan period (centuries before Sri Gupta). Statement 2 is correct: Official Gupta inscriptions consistently name Sri Gupta as the foundational head of the dynasty. [Primary Reference: Upinder Singh, A History of Ancient and Early Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the term 'Maharaja' used by early Guptas:
1. It signified complete paramount sovereignty and supreme military command over all of Aryavarta.
2. In the hierarchical polity of the time, it denoted a feudatory or subordinate ruler under a greater paramount power.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect: Paramount sovereignty was denoted by 'Maharajadhiraja'. Statement 2 is correct: 'Maharaja' was typically held by minor local rulers or feudatories before the family attained imperial independence. [Primary Reference: D.C. Sircar, Indian Epigraphy]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements concerning the geographic and economic context of Sri Gupta's reign:
1. The initial core area of the Guptas gave them access to iron ore resources of Chotanagpur plateau, aiding metallurgical development.
2. Sri Gupta's domain had zero interaction with overseas trade networks or foreign pilgrims.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Proximity to the Chotanagpur plateau provided access to rich iron ore deposits, critical for tools and weaponry expansion in the Gupta era. Statement 2 is incorrect: I-tsing's account proves direct engagement with foreign Buddhist pilgrims from China during Sri Gupta's time. [Primary Reference: R.S. Sharma, Indian Feudalism]
